title: CHAPTER 2 : NUMBER SYSTEM – ULTRA CONCEPT + TRICKS + FORMULA EDITION

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Number classification forms the foundational base for all arithmetic and algebraic problem-solving.
Divisibility rules and remainder theorems significantly reduce calculation time during competitive exams.
HCF and LCM operations are key to solving periodic events, ratio problems, and fraction simplifications.
Unit digit cyclicity allows rapid determination of trailing digits in large exponential numbers.
Digital root (casting out nines) and base systems provide essential shortcuts for option elimination in exams.

blocks.content: The number system is the foundation of quantitative aptitude. It helps students understand how numbers behave, how they can be manipulated, and how patterns can be identified quickly.
A strong command over the number system improves speed in simplification, algebra, percentages, and data interpretation.This chapter must be mastered conceptually rather than memorized superficially.
Numbers are broadly classified as follows:

items:
• Natural Numbers: Counting numbers starting from 1.
  • Whole Numbers: Natural numbers including zero.
  • Integers: Positive numbers, negative numbers, and zero.
  • Rational Numbers: Numbers expressible as p/q where q ≠ 0.
  • Irrational Numbers: Numbers that cannot be expressed as fractions (√2, π).
  • Real Numbers: Combination of rational and irrational numbers.
Natural Numbers: Counting numbers starting from 1.
Whole Numbers: Natural numbers including zero.
Integers: Positive numbers, negative numbers, and zero.
Rational Numbers: Numbers expressible as p/q where q ≠ 0.
Irrational Numbers: Numbers that cannot be expressed as fractions (√2, π).
Real Numbers: Combination of rational and irrational numbers.

blocks.content: Every integer is rational, but not every rational number is an integer.
Prime numbers have exactly two factors — 1 and itself. Examples: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.

items: 2 is the only even prime.
1 is neither prime nor composite.
Every prime greater than 3 is of the form 6n ± 1.

blocks.content: Trick:To check if a number is prime, test divisibility only up to its square root.
Divisible by 3 → Sum of digits divisible by 3. Divisible by 4 → Last two digits divisible by 4. Divisible by 5 → Ends in 0 or 5.
Divisible by 6 → Divisible by both 2 and 3.
Divisible by 8 → Last three digits divisible by 8.
Divisible by 9 → Sum of digits divisible by 9.
Divisible by 11 → Difference between alternate digit sums is 0 or multiple of 11.
Speed Trick: Always check divisibility before attempting long division.
